leads.summary: Provider test models every older provider as a guaranteed conflict and cannot exercise a non-conflicting provider
leads.consequence: The fake -S treats any package whose installed name is not gpu-screen-recorder as if the transaction necessarily removes it when --ask 4 is present, and overwrites the fake name with the canonical package. Pacman's --ask 4 merely accepts an actual conflict-removal question; it cannot make a package with no declared conflict disappear. A third-party provider with disjoint paths could remain installed alongside a newly added canonical recorder while the postcheck prefers the canonical name and the migration is marked done, or shared files could make the transaction fail and retry. The named AUR gpu-screen-recorder-git explicitly declares conflicts, so the named test case is faithful; third-party providers are a hypothesis. Add a no-conflict provider fixture or narrow the comment/claim to conflicting providers; a real non-conflicting provider package and file list would settle the runtime impact.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** The rc and stable channels do not offer `gpu-screen-recorder>=6.1.2` yet, so once this migration reaches them it cannot finish and stops every `omarchy update`.

### Migration fails while the channel lacks 6.1.2

On 2026-10-01 the rc and stable mirrors serve 6.1.0-1 (edge: 6.1.3-1), so `pacman -S` reports `target not found` and the migration exits 1. `omarchy-migrate` stops at the first failure, so later migrations and the rest of `omarchy update` are skipped each run. **Impact:** rc machines upgraded with `omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro` take `omarchy-dev` from edge and would hit this with the first build after merge; other rc and stable installs would, if a release reaches them first.

**Suggested change:** Ship once each channel's mirror has 6.1.2+, or skip with a message when `pacman -Sp "gpu-screen-recorder>=6.1.2"` finds no candidate (a skipped `-git` build is not revisited).

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at b0477ee)</summary>

# Reproducer: the migration stops `omarchy-migrate` on channels that do not offer gpu-screen-recorder 6.1.2 yet

Reviewed head: `b0477ee6ee81bf04dd81c35dc86e9da3cc55ec0e` (omacom/omarchy PR #11558).

## 1. What the channels serve (checked 2026-10-01T03:17Z)

These read-only commands list the `gpu-screen-recorder` entries in each channel's repository database. Actual output:

```text
$ curl -fsS https://rc-mirror.omarchy.org/extra/os/x86_64/extra.db | tar -tzf - | grep '^gpu-screen-recorder-[0-9].*/$'
gpu-screen-recorder-6.1.0-1/
$ curl -fsS https://stable-mirror.omarchy.org/extra/os/x86_64/extra.db | tar -tzf - | grep '^gpu-screen-recorder-[0-9].*/$'
gpu-screen-recorder-6.1.0-1/
$ curl -fsS https://mirror.omarchy.org/extra/os/x86_64/extra.db | tar -tzf - | grep '^gpu-screen-recorder-[0-9].*/$'
gpu-screen-recorder-6.1.3-1/
$ curl -fsS https://pkgs.omarchy.org/rc/x86_64/omarchy.db | tar --zstd -tf - | grep '^gpu-screen-recorder-[0-9].*/$'
gpu-screen-recorder-5.12.3-2/
```

The rc and stable Arch mirrors serve 6.1.0-1 (their `extra.db` was last modified on 2026-09-07 and 2026-09-08). The `[omarchy]` repository serves 5.12.3-2. Only the edge mirror has a release at or above 6.1.2.

## 2. Test in the PR's own style

Save as `test/shell.d/gpu-screen-recorder-unavailable-test.sh` at the PR head and run `bash test/shell.d/gpu-screen-recorder-unavailable-test.sh`. The `pacman -S` stub answers like pacman does when no sync package satisfies a versioned target: it prints `error: target not found: <target>` and exits 1. In pacman's source, `resolvedep()` in `lib/libalpm/deps.c` returns no package, then `process_group()` in `src/pacman/sync.c` prints `target not found: %s` and returns 1. Everything else is the PR's migration unchanged.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

# Reproducer for migrations/1789156273.sh on a channel whose repositories do not
# offer gpu-screen-recorder>=6.1.2 yet. Place it in test/shell.d/ and run it with
# bash. The pacman stub answers -S the way pacman does when no sync package
# satisfies a versioned target: "error: target not found: <target>", status 1.
# REPO_VERSION is what the rc and stable Arch mirrors served on 2026-10-01.

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

migration="$ROOT/migrations/1789156273.sh"
test_tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_tmp"' EXIT

stub_bin="$test_tmp/bin"
mkdir -p "$stub_bin"

cat >"$stub_bin/pacman" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash

printf 'pacman %s\n' "$*" >>"$PACMAN_LOG"
case "$1" in
  -Q)
    printf '%s %s\n' "$INSTALLED_NAME" "$INSTALLED_VERSION"
    ;;
  -T)
    exit 0
    ;;
  -S)
    target=${!#}
    if (( $(vercmp "$REPO_VERSION" "${target#*>=}") < 0 )); then
      echo "error: target not found: $target" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    ;;
  *)
    exit 2
    ;;
esac
STUB

cat >"$stub_bin/sudo" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash

exec "$@"
STUB

chmod +x "$stub_bin/pacman" "$stub_bin/sudo"

stopped=()
for installed in "gpu-screen-recorder 6.1.0-1" "gpu-screen-recorder-git 6.1.1.r1.gdeadbeef-1"; do
  : >"$test_tmp/pacman.log"
  status=0
  INSTALLED_NAME=${installed% *} INSTALLED_VERSION=${installed#* } REPO_VERSION=6.1.0-1 \
    PACMAN_LOG="$test_tmp/pacman.log" PATH="$stub_bin:/usr/bin" \
    bash -euo pipefail "$migration" >"$test_tmp/output" 2>&1 || status=$?

  printf -- '--- installed: %s, repository offers: 6.1.0-1\n' "$installed"
  cat "$test_tmp/pacman.log" "$test_tmp/output"
  printf 'migration exit status: %s\n' "$status"

  (( status == 0 )) || stopped+=("$installed")
done

(( ${#stopped[@]} == 0 )) ||
  fail "the migration does not stop omarchy-migrate while the channel lacks v6.1.2" "stopped for: ${stopped[*]}"
pass "the migration does not stop omarchy-migrate while the channel lacks v6.1.2"
```

## 3. Actual output at the reviewed head

stdout:

```text
--- installed: gpu-screen-recorder 6.1.0-1, repository offers: 6.1.0-1
pacman -Q gpu-screen-recorder
pacman -S --noconfirm --needed gpu-screen-recorder>=6.1.2
Upgrade GPU Screen Recorder to v6.1.2 or newer
error: target not found: gpu-screen-recorder>=6.1.2
migration exit status: 1
--- installed: gpu-screen-recorder-git 6.1.1.r1.gdeadbeef-1, repository offers: 6.1.0-1
pacman -Q gpu-screen-recorder
pacman -S --noconfirm --ask 4 --needed gpu-screen-recorder>=6.1.2
Upgrade GPU Screen Recorder to v6.1.2 or newer
error: target not found: gpu-screen-recorder>=6.1.2
migration exit status: 1
```

stderr:

```text
stopped for: gpu-screen-recorder 6.1.0-1 gpu-screen-recorder-git 6.1.1.r1.gdeadbeef-1
not ok - the migration does not stop omarchy-migrate while the channel lacks v6.1.2
```

Exit status: 1.

## 4. What exit status 1 does to the queue

`bin/omarchy-migrate` runs under `set -euo pipefail` and calls each pending migration with `bash -euo pipefail "$file"` (lines 88 to 97). The marker is written only after that call succeeds, so the first failing migration ends the run before its marker or any later migration. The existing test `test/shell.d/migrate-scope-test.sh` (lines 56 to 77) already checks that a failing migration makes the runner exit non-zero and leaves no marker. `omarchy update` runs `omarchy-migrate` under `set -e`, so the rest of the update is skipped too.

</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Sequence on rc/stable today:** the `[omarchy]` repository serves 5.12.3-2, so no repository satisfies `>=6.1.2`. The failure applies to both the packaged recorder and `-git` providers. `bin/omarchy-migrate` writes a migration's marker only after it exits 0 and stops at the first failure, and `omarchy update` runs it under `set -e`. A legacy rc install running `omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro` would end with "Upgrade incomplete" on each rerun until the mirror moves. A default ISO build uses the stable mirror, so the new acceptance check would also fail there today.

**Verified** (pacman 7.1.0 source and sandbox tests):
- `pacman -Q` returns a provider such as `gpu-screen-recorder-git`, and the name and version split handles it; `-git` versions such as `6.1.2.r1.g…` compare as intended with `vercmp`.
- `pkg>=ver` is a supported `-S` target, `--needed` does not block provider replacement, and `--ask 4` answers only the conflict-removal question.
- Absent recorders are left alone; an unreadable package database keeps the migration pending.
- The new test passes at the head (8 of 8) and with the PR's files on current `quattro`.

**Optional notes:**
- **Same migration filename as #11523.** Open PR #11523 adds a different `migrations/1789156273.sh`. Migration markers are keyed by file name, so whichever lands second needs a new timestamp.
- **IgnorePkg is overridden** (source reading, not run). For an explicit `-S` target pacman asks "Install anyway?" for an ignored package and `--noconfirm` answers yes, so a pinned recorder gets upgraded while `-Syu` respects the pin. Checking `pacman-conf IgnorePkg` first would preserve the pin, if that is wanted.
- **Optional test improvement:** the test's `pacman -S` stub installs `PACKAGE_UPGRADE_VERSION` regardless of the constraint or repository contents, so the realistic failure above is never exercised, and the "remains below v6.1.2" case simulates a pacman success that cannot happen for a `>=6.1.2` target. A stub that returns `target not found` would cover it (see the reproducer).

</details>
